surfaces.part: terrain tile: sand strip on left and dark teal water fill

answer.evidence: This is a full 16x16 autotile terrain tile: a sand/shore strip along the left columns and dark teal water across the rest. Column scans show one continuous run over rows 0-15 with no eave, no edge line and no ellipse. It is a flat ground tile viewed from above, not a standing object. It has no front face and no top-surface band.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate on the board is a tiny dark teal square with a thin brown strip down its left edge. It is far smaller than the 4x3-tile ground patch the references show, so it does not read as the same kind of piece. By eye it shows about 2-3 visible tones: a mostly uniform teal fill with a brown edge line. It has no sand grain, speckle or clumps. The measured 25% near-flat coverage matches the flat teal block, while both references are at 0%. The measured 10 tones per tile is not visible on the board, so I did not credit it. There is no real outline (0% neutral dark edge pixels, but also no tinted outline). The grass reference carries clumps, tufts and several greens, and the paving reference has shaded stones, so the candidate looks much flatter and thinner than both.
